operator_io_quirks: langs has exactly 1 row (lid=1, lang='ca', locale='ca_ES'); every FK to langs collapses to a single value, so child tables are effectively single-language.
pages_words has 129M rows and biwords 21M: read_schema must rowid-sample (max_rows_per_table) or it will hang; original_sizes still needs full count(*).
pages_words.pid distinct=336 and wid distinct=53644 in samples but table has 129M rows: distinct counts are from the sampled slice, not the full table.
langs_words, pages_words, biwords are WITHOUT ROWID composite-PK tables; rowid-based sampling (rowid % k) is invalid there — need a fallback (e.g. ORDER BY pk LIMIT).
AUTOINCREMENT on langs.lid, pages.pid, words.wid: inserting explicit PK values is fine, but the sqlite_sequence table exists in the DDL clone and must be tolerated.

Five triggers (ins_page/del_page/ins_lang_word/del_lang_word/ins_page_word/del_page_word) fire on INSERT and UPDATE langs.pages/words counters; TS inserts will mutate langs.pages/words away from the original 1129144/2764996.

pages has UNIQUE(lid,page,title) — a 3-column unique constraint, not a single-column unique; upstream's line-based 'unique' scan will mark the first token of that line (lid) as unique, which is wrong.
langs.lang and langs.locale are single-column UNIQUE; words.word is UNIQUE; with 1-row langs, drop_unique_duplicates will keep at most 1 row in langs.
pages.title samples are accented Catalan words (Àbac, Addicció) — text storage, no date-like strings; declared TEXT dispatches to String fuzzer.
All declared types are INTEGER or TEXT; no date/time/bool/bit/year columns, so Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers are never exercised here.
pages.lid FK to langs(lid) with ON UPDATE/DELETE CASCADE; langs has 1 row so pages.lid is always 1 in the original — TS will draw from the (filtered) langs.lid column.
biwords has two FKs to words (w1st, w2nd) — same parent table twice; fill_foreign_keys_consistently must handle two child columns drawing from the same parent column independently.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all INTEGER columns: uniform in [-10^scale, 10^scale] with scale from type args (none here -> default), then +-1/+-2 perturbation; produces huge values far from the original 1..2.7M range.

String fuzzer on lang/locale/title/word: random a-zA-Z 0-9() strings of length 0..20 with 50% contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop char); 'ca_ES' style locales and accented Catalan titles will not be reproduced.
langs gets size 1..~2500 by choose_table_sizes; with 1 original row and UNIQUE lang/locale, drop_unique_duplicates will cut it to 1 row, so pages.lid FK has a single parent value.

pages_words and biwords are huge in the original but TS sizes them like any table (<=2500 rows), so joins that in the original return millions of rows return a handful — a likely FP source for aggregate/count queries.

Composite PKs (langs_words, pages_words, biwords) get max_l0=30 fresh draws per member; sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate PK tuples, so the effective row count is far below the requested size.
FK columns draw from the parent's FINAL filtered column with replacement; with langs=1 row, pages.lid, langs_words.lid, biwords.lid are all 1, so any query grouping by language sees one group.

Triggers increment langs.pages/words on every inserted page/lang_word; TS-inserted langs.pages/words will not match the original 1129144/2764996, so queries comparing pages count to langs.pages will disagree — likely FN/FP driver.
words.word UNIQUE with random strings: collisions rare, but drop_unique_duplicates keeps ~all rows; word values are implausible ('aB3()x') so LIKE/equality on real words fails — FN driver.

pages UNIQUE(lid,page,title): upstream marks lid as unique (line-based scan), so drop_unique_duplicates may keep only 1 page row — a severe under-population of pages, likely FP for count/join queries.
No date/time columns: Date/Time fuzzers unused; any gold SQL with date literals would rely on the literal pool only.
pages.revision and pages.page are INTEGER with distinct=200000 in samples; TS Number fuzzer will produce values outside the original 1..200000 / 24M..28M ranges — implausible for range predicates.
